    Dune: Global-Null max-F Contrasts

    dune-maxT.Rmd

    The Dune meadow data provide a compact example of simultaneous pairwise location tests. This analysis treats Management as the sole fixed factor and uses Bray–Curtis dissimilarities.

    data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")
design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management,
  dune.env,
  vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
)

    permanova_maxT_pairwise() calculates all Management contrasts from one shared raw-observation permutation stream. For each arrangement it retains the largest pairwise pseudo-F. A contrast’s adjusted p-value is the proportion of those maxima at least as large as its observed pseudo-F.

    fit <- permanova_maxT_pairwise(
  design,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260719
)
fit
#> Global-null max-F distance contrasts
#> Family: all pairwise one-factor centroid contrasts 
#> Error control: weak familywise error control under the complete equal-centroid null; strong control is not claimed 
#>  contrast df        ss denominator_df  pseudo_f p_perm p_maxT
#>   BF - HF  1 0.1617135             16 0.9141421  0.415  0.880
#>   BF - NM  1 0.5662456             16 3.2009023  0.030  0.090
#>   BF - SF  1 0.4016624             16 2.2705377  0.075  0.205
#>   HF - NM  1 0.6513088             16 3.6817517  0.005  0.035
#>   HF - SF  1 0.2828804             16 1.5990807  0.165  0.505
#>   NM - SF  1 0.7575728             16 4.2824464  0.010  0.015
#>                  error_control
#>  weak FWER under complete null
#>  weak FWER under complete null
#>  weak FWER under complete null
#>  weak FWER under complete null
#>  weak FWER under complete null
#>  weak FWER under complete null

    The raw and max-F columns answer different questions.

    fit$table[, c("contrast", "pseudo_f", "p_perm", "p_maxT")]
#>         contrast  pseudo_f p_perm p_maxT
#> BF - HF  BF - HF 0.9141421  0.415  0.880
#> BF - NM  BF - NM 3.2009023  0.030  0.090
#> BF - SF  BF - SF 2.2705377  0.075  0.205
#> HF - NM  HF - NM 3.6817517  0.005  0.035
#> HF - SF  HF - SF 1.5990807  0.165  0.505
#> NM - SF  NM - SF 4.2824464  0.010  0.015
fit$error_control
#> [1] "weak familywise error control under the complete equal-centroid null; strong control is not claimed"

    The scope statement is essential: raw permutation is justified by the complete null that every Management centroid is equal. The maximum provides weak familywise error control under that complete null. It does not guarantee strong control when some Management contrasts are truly nonzero and others remain null. Use Holm-adjusted permanova_pairwise() when strong familywise control is required without a separately justified subset-pivotal argument.

    Planned contrast families use the same shared distribution:

    planned <- rbind(
  `BF - HF` = c(BF = 1, HF = -1, NM = 0, SF = 0),
  `managed - unmanaged` = c(BF = 1/3, HF = 1/3, NM = -1, SF = 1/3)
)
permanova_maxT(
  design, planned, permutations = 199, seed = 20260719
)$table
#>                                contrast df        ss denominator_df  pseudo_f
#> BF - HF                         BF - HF  1 0.1617135             16 0.9141421
#> managed - unmanaged managed - unmanaged  1 0.8784454             16 4.9657209
#>                     p_perm p_maxT                 error_control
#> BF - HF              0.415   0.65 weak FWER under complete null
#> managed - unmanaged  0.010   0.01 weak FWER under complete null

    Mixed models and multifactor nuisance adjustments are intentionally rejected: their complete-null exchangeability and studentizing denominators require design-specific simultaneous-inference contracts.
